claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi nanoalloys have a critical temperature within 600–1200 K.
Atomic jump-path multiplicity increases markedly near this critical temperature.
Enhanced atomic jump multiplicity promotes local chemical ordering.
The resulting local chemical ordering stabilizes both the structure and chemistry of the alloy at high temperatures.
The initial simulated CoCrFeMnNi state is equilibrated, chemically disordered, and has randomized local chemical environments.
Molecular dynamics coupled with neural network kinetics can quantify atomic jump multiplicity and track local chemical-order evolution.
Sampling from 600 K to 1200 K is sufficient to capture the relevant jump pathways and the proposed critical behavior.
Local chemical ordering in CoCrFeMnNi is mediated by heterogeneous diffusion characterized by variable atomic jump multiplicity.
The temperature dependence of atomic jump multiplicity is non-monotonic.
Increased jump multiplicity drives heterogeneous diffusion that locally organizes atoms into ordered arrangements.
Heterogeneous diffusion produces greater stability than homogeneous diffusion.
The simulations will exhibit a distinct peak in diffusion heterogeneity concurrent with enhanced local chemical ordering at one temperature between 600 K and 1200 K.
The ordered state will correlate with energy or structure-retention markers of structural and chemical stability.
Diffusion will be more uniform at temperatures below and above the proposed critical regime.
Homogeneous diffusion without a jump-multiplicity peak results in weaker local chemical ordering and lower high-temperature stability.
Changing alloy composition or adding elements may shift the critical temperature or change the magnitude of the effect.
A refractory NbMoTa alloy exhibits maximum B2 order at a critical temperature and maximum diffusion heterogeneity near that temperature.
Random jumps have equal path probabilities, whereas directional non-random jumps are dominated by one path.
Failure to observe a non-monotonic multiplicity peak correlated with enhanced local ordering would falsify the hypothesis.
